## Summary

`query()` now sends the user's SQL as written and passes its `format` to
the server as the `default_format` setting, instead of trimming the
query, stripping trailing semicolons and appending `\nFORMAT <format>`.

It fixes the problems caused by the appended clause:

- a semicolon followed by a comment (`SELECT 1; -- note`) no longer
fails with `Multi-statements are not allowed` (#973);
- `FORMAT` is no longer placed after a trailing `SETTINGS` clause
(#970);
- the short `SHOW ROW POLICIES` syntax works (#759).

`command()` and `exec()` also send the SQL as written, except `exec()`
with `values`, where trailing semicolons are still removed because the
server reads the data right after the statement.

## Observable changes

- The `format` option overrides a `default_format` in
`clickhouse_settings`.
- The query text in `system.query_log`, logs and traces no longer ends
with `FORMAT`.
- **A `FORMAT` clause inside a `query()` query:** the server prefers it
over `default_format`, so the response could be parsed with the wrong
format. `query()` now compares the `X-ClickHouse-Format` response header
with the `format` option and throws an error naming both when they
differ. A matching clause is accepted. Statements without output do not
send the header and are unaffected. (Before, this was always a
duplicate-`FORMAT` syntax error.)
- **A user profile that locks `default_format`** (a `<constraints>`
entry) now fails every `query()` with `SETTING_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION`,
because `default_format` is sent on every request. Seen on 26.10 and
26.11; 24.8 and 23.8 reject `default_format` in a profile, so it cannot
happen there. Mentioned in the changelogs and covered by an integration
test.
- **An `X-ClickHouse-Format` request header** set via `http_headers`
(client or call level) is not sent by `query()`: the server prefers it
over `default_format` (and, on 26.8+, over an inline `FORMAT`), so it
would make the response unparseable. The other methods send it as given.
- **Errors on 24.8:** an error raised before execution comes back
through the JSON-family output formats (`{"exception": ...}`, a whole
document with an `exception` key, `["..."]`, ...), where it used to be
plain text because the appended `FORMAT` was inside the query that
failed to parse. `parseError()` now extracts the text so
`ClickHouseError.message` keeps no JSON escaping. Plain-text formats
(CSV, TSV, Parquet, ...) are unaffected. The same applies, on every
version, to an error raised while the result is written
(`http_write_exception_in_output_format`): the exception row then comes
after the column names, types and data rows, and `parseError()` picks
the first candidate that parses as a ClickHouse error.
